newsitem.title: USA: Cattaraugus County, N.Y., rated Baa1 by Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Cattaraugus County, N.Y., rated Baa1 by Moody's.

text.p: MOODY'S ASSIGNS A Baa1 TO THE COUNTY'S UPCOMING SALE
Cattaraugus (County of) NY
County
New York
Moody's Rating
Issue Public Improvement (Serial) Bonds, 1997
Rating Baa1
Sale Amount $9,040,000.00
Expected Sale Date 07/16/97
Rating Description General Obligation

NEW YORK, July 15, 1997 -- Moody's Investors Service has assigned a Baa1 to the county's general obligation debt. The rating reflects our expectation of continued satisfactory financial performance, supported by a growing, but still somewhat limited economic base. Although recent litigation raises concerns over the potential lose on a portion of the county's tax base, the rating outlook remains stable based on our assessment that county is well-positioned to manage the financial impact. The county is offering $9.0 million general obligation bonds and $1.6 million unrated bond anticipation notes for public bid.
SATISFACTORY FINANCIAL POSITION, ALTHOUGH LITIGATION MAY POSE FINANCIAL CHALLENGES.

Financial position is expected to remain stable in the near-term based on positive underlying financial trends and successful renewal of the 1% sales and use tax for an additional two years. The county faces recent litigation concerning its ability to levy property taxes in the City of Salamanca, which may lead to significant loss of property tax revenues. Under the worst case scenario, the county could lose up to $900,000 in annual tax revenues, which represents 3.8% of the 1997 levy, as well as owe a one-time payment of back taxes estimated at $2.8 million. The county is relatively well-positioned to handle these potential loses, given the remaining margin under the property tax rate limit and current reserve levels. General Fund balance was $7.9 million or 10.7% in 1996 and balanced operations are expected in 1997.
GROWING BUT LIMITED ECONOMIC BASE.

The county's taxable valuation continues to grow, enhanced primarily to periodic revaluation as well as some new retail development. This development has fueled retail sales growth and helped to diversify the county's relatively limited economic base, composed primarily of agriculture, winter tourism, and some industrial manufacturing. Other economic indicators post positive results, including some recent improvement in relatively high unemployment rates and stable social services/welfare caseloads. Wealth indicators, however, are below upstate New York regional economic norms.
DEBT LEVELS EXPECTED TO REMAIN MANAGEABLE .

Debt position is expected to improve, given the county's limited future borrowing plans and rapid payout of outstanding debt, with almost 66% retired in ten years. The county has been a frequent issuer in recent years, borrowing for several major facilities as well as annual road and equipment. Debt burden is above average at 4.8% as compared to the 2.3% median. Inclusive of estimated state school building aid to overlapping school districts, debt burden decreases to a more moderate 3.8%. OUTLOOK:

The rating outlook is stable based on the expectation of the county's ability to continue to maintain sound financial operations, despite recent litigation concerning a portion of the tax base in the City of Salamanca, as well as continued economic stability. ANALYSTS:
